About Elveo

Elveo is what happens when two pioneers in direct-to-device (D2D) communications join forces. Elveo brings together a combined 20 years of expertise to close the coverage gap for more than 50 mobile network operators (MNOs) and major distribution partners operating in 60+ countries worldwide.

That heritage and our technology powers what we call ‘elevated intelligence’ — a new approach that processes and adapts on orbit, delivering voice and data services straight to mobile users, IoT devices and machines across enterprise, government and humanitarian sectors worldwide.

As a team, we’re on a mission to deliver powerful compute and connectivity directly to individuals and objects everywhere on Earth.

Join us, and become part of a globally inclusive company that is transforming satellite communications from a niche service to an essential global infrastructure, and democratizing connectivity for billions worldwide.

Ready to take the next step? Join us.

 


JOB SUMMARY

Elveo, a direct-to-device satellite communications company, is hiring an Embedded Linux Platform Engineer in Chantilly, VA. You will own the custom Yocto-based Linux distribution that runs on our spacecraft computers, along with the build, CI, SDK, and update infrastructure that the rest of engineering relies on.

Our flight software runs on a custom embedded Linux distribution that we build in-house with Yocto/OpenEmbedded for multiple ARM and x86 platforms. You will own it end to end: recipes and layers, BSP and kernel integration, the CI system that builds it, the SDKs other teams develop against, and the architecture for updating systems already in orbit.

Your users are the flight software, payload, and hardware engineers who build on what you ship.


CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own our Yocto/OpenEmbedded distribution across multiple ARM and x86 targets: recipes, custom layers, and distro, machine, and image configuration.

 - Maintain BSP integration, kernel configuration, and device trees; qualify boot, storage, and peripheral behavior for flight.

 - Own the distribution’s CI pipelines: build infrastructure, caching, build times, reproducibility, and artifact publishing.

 - Build and maintain SDKs and toolchains for teams that develop against the platform, including kernel driver development.

 - Architect and advise on how on-orbit systems are updated: robust update and rollback mechanisms, and update sizes suited to constrained communication links.

 - Define the OS-level contract flight software builds against: service management, filesystem layout, watchdogs, logging, and time synchronization.

 - Partner with flight software and hardware engineers on issues that cross the application/platform boundary.


BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

 - Several years building and maintaining embedded Linux systems for products that shipped to the field.

 - Hands-on Yocto/OpenEmbedded experience: writing recipes and bbappends, maintaining custom layers, and understanding the separation between distro, machine, and image configuration.

 - Comfort in the Linux kernel: configuration, device trees, driver and boot debugging.

 - Proficiency in C; fluency in Python and shell scripting.

 - Experience with bootloaders, systemd, and root filesystem design.

 - Experience owning or substantially building CI pipelines for embedded software.

 - A bachelor’s degree or higher in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Maintaining a distribution across several hardware targets at once.

 - Vendor BSP integration.

 - Yocto SDK/eSDK generation, including support for out-of-tree kernel modules.

 - A/B or over-the-air update systems (e.g., Mender, RAUC, SWUpdate, OSTree), ideally over bandwidth-constrained links.

 - Shared build caches, distributed builds, or reproducible builds at scale.

 - Real-time Linux (PREEMPT_RT): kernel configuration, latency measurement and tuning, CPU and interrupt isolation, and thread priority management for critical workloads.

 - Bringing real-time cores (e.g., Zephyr, FreeRTOS) on heterogeneous SoCs into a shared build, CI, and update pipeline alongside Linux.

 - Upgrading across Yocto LTS releases.

 - Packaging Rust or containerized applications in embedded Linux images.

 - Secure boot, signed images, and read-only root filesystems.

 - Prior work on space, defense, medical, or other systems where physical access to a deployed device is impossible.


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

 - To comply with U.S. Government export control regulations (ITAR), applicants must be one of the following: (i) a U.S. citizen or national, (ii) a lawful permanent resident (green card holder), (iii) a refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) an asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158. Individuals who do not meet these criteria must be eligible to obtain the necessary authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

 - Learn about ITAR here: https://www.pmddtc.state.gov


JOB LOCATION

Chantilly, VA. On-site.
